8/2/2026
Dog was closed to back half of kennel during AM cleaning.  Had a relaxed & wiggly body while leashing.  Pulled hard on leash to small PY.  Would pull hard towards kenneled dogs while barking attempting to fence fight, handler would use leash pressure to guide dog away from kennel gates.  Once in PY, dog would approach both handlers with a relaxed body.  Appears to know "SIT" for treats & would take treats gently.  Allows all petting with no skin crawling.  Picked up leash & walked with a strong pull on leash.  While walking past main PY, this dog would pull hard towards fence line while dog in PY would start to bark towards fence, handler asked for alternate dog to be walked to opposite side of PY due to amount of reactivity this dog displayed.  Used leash to guide dog away & continue to walk.  Would not enter into kennel on own or with treats.  Would attempt to fence fight with neighboring kennel.  Handler opened kennel divider, would not enter into kennel still.  Assistant handler would use sort board to assist in guiding dog into kennel while dog would continue to pull towards neighboring kennel.  Once dog entered into kennel, waited a few moments for dog to settle then removed leash by hand.
8/1/2026
Dog was at front of kennel, soft face, gentle wagging tail. Easy to leash, allowed handler to pet on top of head and adjust leash around E-collar. Dog exited kennel, initially appeared calm, then immediately began fence fighting with reactive neighbor. Handler called dog, used moderate leash pressure to guide away. Dog broke focus, walked with handler but remained tense, chuffing. In hallway, dog began growling, whining, pulling towards kennel wing windows. Handler used continuous verbal coaxing and light pressure on short leash to keep dog moving. Walked dog outside, dog was on alert, growling. Handler could not navigate to J-yard due to blockage, turned around and started returning in original direction. Dog froze, leaned body weight against handler, would not move. Handler coaxed dog on, lightly pushed legs back against dog. Dog began walking. Intense growling when passing dogs in I-building. Handler walked dog back inside. Second handler joined to assist. Dog leaned against first handler again, tense body. Handler petted dog, tried soft vocal coaxing. Dog would look up and stare at handler, did not soften, tail tucked. Second handler called to dog from up ahead, dog followed. Dog was tense, walked slowly. Handlers exited into main hallway, dog began growling and whining when hearing dogs nearby. Due to inside area being highly populated with staff and customers and no clear path to outside yards, handlers opted to return dog to kennel. Dog remained tense, low growled continuously when passing other dogs. Second handler closed out neighbors. First handler led dog back to kennel, dog continued to growl. Would not enter kennel. Handler attempted to guide dog into kennel with leash pressure, dog resisted. Second handler used sort board to guide dog inside. Leash removed via clip lead.

Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers,without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 8/9/26. Dog was closed outside for cleaning, at front of kennel, panting, neutral body. Wagged tail when spoken to. Easy to leash, pushed quickly out of kennel. Walked with moderate pull, alert to neighboring dogs but did not attempt to engage. Walked to main play yard without issue. In yard, dog remained on alert to surroundings, ears forward, chuffing. Explored on own for a few moments, patrolling fence line. Eventually came to handlers when called, soft face, wagging tail. Allowed all petting, leaned in for it. Grabby with treats. Handlers sat on bench, dog ran over and jumped onto bench between them, began rolling around against handlers, wide open mouth, wagging tail, seeking attention. Allowed all petting, very affiliative. After a few moments, another dog was walked outside of yard. This dog became very alert, forward posture, jumped from bench and charged fence, tense body, tail flagged. Appeared to lose sight of other dog but remained focused on corner of fence, chuffing. Dog began jumping up against fence as if to jump out of yard. Handlers approached, got dog's attention, retrieved leash without issue. On return, dog walked with moderate pull. Saw another dog a few yards ahead, stood still beside handler, tense body, watching. When handler began walking dog towards building, dog pulled hard in direction of other dog, needed moderate leash pressure to guide away. Handler kept leash short, used verbal coaxing while walking past kenneled dogs. This dog was alert but did not attempt to engage. Entered own kennel with light guidance, allowed leash removal by hand.
7/31/2026
Dog was closed out for AM cleaning. Dog was standing at front of kennel; neutral body; offered treat; gave brief tail wags; took treat gently; easy leash; exited; walked well; light pull towards reactive dog; stiff; tail hackles raised; continued walking with light leash pressure; walked well; light pull at times. Took to lower yard; explored briefly; approached handler; jumped up once; approached assistant handler on bench; leaned into petting; leaned over onto side; laid on side across assistant handler's feet; open mouth; relaxed; placed front paws on handler's lap; easy to redirect off; sought attention; jumped up onto bench; got down; allowed for all petting; turned onto back; continued to allow for all petting. Dog reactive towards all dogs in passing to kennel, lunging and biting at fence, hesitant to enter kennel but able to be guided into kennel with leash, used clip leash for leash retrieval. When kennel door was shut dog would jump onto door with high arousal, eyes wide, flagged tail, tense body.

Stoic, not soliciting attention, softened in triage, allowed petting, leaning in for petting, rolling over on side, tail slightly wagging, allowed all handling and vaccines with muzzle wrap restraint, walked to kennel, strong pull, stop and go in kennel wing, tail flagging, hackles raised, fence fighting, slow leash removal. sections.evaluation_comments:
8/6/2026
Updating color due to NHO status.
8/6/2026
Patient approached front of kennel with calm body when verbally coaxed.
8/2/2026
Handler approached kennel front, dog initially alarm barked with tense posture, handler tossed treat into kennel and dog loosened. Handler lured dog over to other side of kennel for easier leashing. Dog had low head carry when peeking through portal before entering back kennel and alarm barked again. Once handler lowered guillotine and continued offering treats dog loosened in posture. Handler was able to drape leash over head with minimal difficulty. Once leash was secure handler opened gate, dog exited and began walking pass occupied kennels, dogs began barking and dog turned away, handler was able to guide dog out of ward avoiding occupied kennels. Once in hallway dog began pulling strongly, dog pulled on entire walk to PY. Once in PY handler began adjusting leash stopper, dog immediately urinated and defecated. Handler was able to lure dog over and allow assistant handler to pick up feces before release. Handler then released dog. Dog is highly food motivated, dog muzzle nudged at treat pouch a few times throughout evaluation but never openly mouthed or pulled on pouch. Handlers were able to pet and fully handle dog without issue. Dog showed brief moments of over arousal with heavier petting but was easily able to be redirected. Handlers were able to guide dog down when dog became jumpy. After about 10 minutes of out of kennel time handlers walked dog back to kennel. Dog pulled strongly and showed no reactivity towards occupied kennels. Handler was able to guide dog into kennel easily and offered treat with one hand while remove leash with the other. Handler closed gate and left behind small jackpot. Dog approached handler at front gate with loose posture.
**Review escape attempt and RG notes listed from PO**
8/1/2026
Dog was at front of kennel, dilated pupils, tense body, repetitive hard barking with forward posture, handler tossed treats, dog would stop and sniff them out, handler went to back of kennel for cleaner area to pull from, dog ran up to kennel door, jumping up at door and barking, stopped for treats, remained at door still tense but no barking, wide eyes, handler reached in leash, tossed treats to the ground, able to place leash as dog ate, dog exited, sniffed toward assistant handler, then followed handler out of kennel wing, froze briefly in front of reactive dogs but continued forward with light leash pressure, strong pull to yard, entered catch pen and stopped to urinate, exited catch pen, needed mild coaxing to enter yard, would explore yard as handler held leash, body was neutral, still alert, would take treats with slight tail wag, demonstrated "sit," approached assistant handler and sniffed them then resumed exploring, handler dropped leash to let dog move freely. Assistant would toss tennis balls,dog would show mild interest but not fully engage, turning away to sniff yard, would sniff at handlers treat bag, handler would ask for "sit" and hand feed, dog took treats gently. Dog allowed petting from both handlers, continued to solicit treats and attention, a volunteer and dog walked past yard, this dog ran up to the fence, barking, jumped up at fence, assistant picked up end of leash and walked dog back, once dog was out of sight this dog would pace yard, alert and looking down pathway, handlers would call over with treats and toys, dog eventually settled again, started to play with toys, would chase after them with bouncy gait, picking up and carrying back in front of handlers, assistant would use multiple toys to continue playing without picking up toy from dog, while playing a volunteer walked past yard, dog ran up to fence, barking, tense, able to be called back away briefly by handlers, but then followed volunteer along fence ling, not barking but tense forward posture, volunteer stopped and fed treat through the fence, dog ate gently, disengaged easily as volunteer walked away. Spent a few more minutes receiving attention from handlers, then easily walked into catch pen, allowed handler to pick up leash and add clip leash, strong pull back to kennel, walked in easily and allowed leash removal with clip leash.
7/29/2026
Handler apporached K9 and had owner put on leash and placed dog in kennel. Handler was able to grab leash and walked K9 out to ramp and onto scale. Handler was able to mircochip scan K9. Once handler attempted to place flea/tick medicine onto K9 K9 jumped up and snapped at handler's arm. ACO was able to place control device onto K9 and a squeeze gate was use to administer vaccines, K9 was walked to kennel with control device, used pressure to guide K9 into kennel and was able to remove the leash, and control device without concerns.

8/5/2026
Dog was closed to inside half of kennel.  Would not approach while unlocking kennel gate, sitting still & stoic.  Offered treats once kennel was unlocked, dog would slowly approach gate with head lowered, ears pinned back, quickly took treat then retreated to back corner of kennel, keeping head lowered & whale eyed.  Slowly leaned into kennel to cast large loop leash, dog would jump forward to catch leash in mouth then drop leash while returning back to corner of kennel with head lowered.  Dog would continue to do this with each attempt while staying quiet.  On last attempt to leash, dog would bite leash, drop leash, approach front of kennel while standing with an intense posture, growling while curling lips, raising hackles & flagging tail, keeping head lowered & started to dilate pupils.  Ended attempt to leash due to rising levels of FAS.
8/5/2026
Dog did not eat. Dog hard stared handler when handler approached with tense body.
8/5/2026
Upon kennel approach, k9 came up to handler right away and sat down in front of kennel. Handler presented hand through kennel door to allow k9 to sniff. K9 sniffed handlers hand and got closer to gate. Handler opened kennel and presented leash, k9 allowed handler to leash with no issues and walked out of kennel with no issues. k9 had no interest in passing dogs on the way to clinic. Once in clinic, k9 allowed all petting from handler. Introduced second tech, k9 immediately went up to tech and allowed all petting as well. When it came to spay checking, k9 did not like any form of restraint or muzzle wrapping. Handlers stopped attempt and k9 went back to seeking attention from both handlers. K9 walked back to kennel with no issues and allowed handler to remove leash by hand.
8/4/2026
Laying outside with eyes wide, stoic, would not come forward for treats or coaxing, did come forward when leash was presented but started to back away so divider was closed. Flinched heavily when attempting to place large loop over head, would stand alongside kennel wall hard staring handler, able to place leash and dog exited quickly out of kennel, began thrashing and yelping, settled once outside but began thrashing and yelping when attempting to coax dog away from building, once dog settled easy leash pull to small play yard, tense bodied, tail flagged. Once in yard dog flinched heavily and airsnapped at handler when placing leash stopper, yelped then settled, did not drop leash all of evaluation. Let dog sniff and explore, quickly paced around yard, has moments of hard staring handler. Would tolerate some petting on body but had some skin crawling. Walked back to kennel with easy leash pull, started to thrash and yelp when approaching kennel but settled, walked into kennel on own, used clip leash for leash retrieval.
8/3/2026

Easy leash placement, airsnapped at handlers hand when placing leash stopper once out of kennel, did not make contact. Walked fine until approaching back portion of kennel, began thrashing, yelping, biting towards leash/handler. Used slight leash pressure to guide dog into kennel, dog would continue to thrash and yelp when removing leash via clip leash.

dog immediately approached ASO to sniff. Head shy. When ASO attempted to leash dog would try to hide. ASO eventually able to leash. Once on leash dog yelped. walks on leash, allowed some handling and petting, moderate restraint with muzzle wrap for vaccines, tense, avoidant of handling around upper body and face, some flippant behavior, snapping at handler and flailing when attempting muzzle wrap and handling around face, use caution when handling

sections.memo:
8/7/2026
08/07/26 17:42 Canine has exhibited behaviors consistent with resource guarding in the shelter, with potential for recurrence. Placement with an experienced adopter or New Hope partner is needed by close of business 8/12/26 to provide necessary behavioral and post-adoption support. May be at risk for euthanasia 8/13/26 or sooner if warranted.
Intake
No memos
sections.evaluation_comments:
8/6/2026
Dog was laying on bed as handler approached front of kennel, began low growling and slightly lifting lip into a curl, did not move from bed, dog had multiple resources at front of kennel (food in bowl and high value chew), handler opted to pull from back of kennel, opened guillotine, dog slowly came out, took a few treats tossed into kennel, high value chew was outside as well, dog stood stoic at door, gazing at handler, easily allowed leash placement and exited kennel, moderate pull to yard. Once outside dog explored independently, relieving herself, wandered with neutral body and low tail, did not initially approach handler and would not come when called, handler allowed dog a few minutes to explore, called dog and said "treat," dog came up, sniffed handler then sniffing the ground, allowed petting, walked away while continuing to sniff, shook off, handler tossed treats but dog did not take them, sniffed at handler again then stood perpendicular in front of them, lip licked when handler reached out and pet along side but then walked closer to handler, leaning side against their leg and sat down, allowed all petting while sitting next to handler, once handler stopped petting dog got up and walked away, but returned to handler when called, remained neutral throughout all interactions, softly panting due to heat, low tail, handler adjusted stopper and placed clip leash while petting dog, then stood up and walked dog out of yard, strong pull back to kennel, resisted going back, began backing away on leash, handler walked dog around to front of kennel, dog was still hesitant but entered on her own after a moment, allowed handler to remove leash with clip leash while standing at the front of kennel, mild tension in face. Handler walked away from kennel but returned to close guillotine due to heat, dog stood at front of kennel, did not react to handler greeting through door or adjusting divider.
*Placing Older Children 12+ requirement due to potential resource guarding behaviors. Adopters should be counseled on managing resources in home and avoid taking anything directly from this dog.*
08/07/26 17:35 Updating requirement.
